newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia calls for Mexico to expel FARC spokesman.
newsitem.headline: Colombia calls for Mexico to expel FARC spokesman.

text.p: Armed forces chief Gen. Harold Bedoya accused the international spokesman of Colombia's main guerrilla army of undermining the image of the military and called on Thursday for him to be expelled from Mexico.

"This sinister personality is running around (in Mexico) with outstanding arrest warrants hanging over him undermining the image of this country and that of the armed forces," Bedoya told the Radionet radio network, referring to Marco Leon Calarca, Mexico City-based spokesman for the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC).
"I don't know how a criminal of these criminal organisations can even get a visa to stay in Mexico. But we understand that visa has now expired," Bedoya added.

Calarca declined to comment on the status of his visa but told Reuters in a phone interview that he was carrying out a political and diplomatic mission and denied Bedoya's allegations of links to "terrorist" activities in Colombia.

"We have a political-diplomatic function here in Mexico. We are not involved in any (military) operations," he said. "We have always had a respectful attitude toward Mexican law and do not take any part in Mexico's internal affairs."

Bedoya's blast at Calarca came a week after the governor of violence-torn northwest Antioquia province called for the FARC's international spokesman to face trial in Colombia after allegedly claiming reposnsibility for a bomb attack on the offices of a banana growers' organisation in Medellin.

Calarca told Reuters he had not issued any claim of responsibility, adding: "The FARC's position is clear. We're against terrorist acts which subvert the course of the people's struggle. Our struggle is a people's struggle."

He also rejected suggestions that the FARC, set up as a pro-Soviet guerrilla force in 1964, was organising a seminar on drug-trafficking in Costa Rica this month. He said the event was arranged by the Forum of Sao Paolo, a broad-based organisation of some 140 parties and groups of the legal and armed left in Latin America.
The FARC, a member of the forum, was merely passing on the invitation via its internet mailing list, he said.
